## What the protocol does

NEBNext EM-seq converts a DNA sample into an indexed Illumina-compatible library while encoding cytosine modification state. End repair/dA-tailing and adaptor ligation precede enzymatic protection and deamination.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  D[DNA] --> E[End repair + dA tail]
  E --> A[EM-seq adaptor ligation]
  A --> P[TET2 + T4-BGT protect 5mC/5hmC]
  P --> C[APOBEC converts unmodified C]
  C --> PCR[Q5U amplification + unique dual index]
  PCR --> L[Sequence-ready library]
```

| Output | What it is |
|---|---|
| indexed library tube | amplified molecules ready for Illumina sequencing |
| fragment-analyzer trace | library-size distribution |
| concentration/molarity | pooling input |
| index/sample sheet | demultiplexing key |
| control metrics | evidence for protection/conversion performance |

The [NEB v2 manual](https://www.neb.com/en/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale8015.pdf) states that the assay jointly detects 5mC and 5hmC and does not distinguish them. The site must record whether the original E7120 or v2 E8015 kit was used; their ranges and workflow details differ.

## QC gate

Check library yield, size, adapter dimer, cycle count, unique-dual-index assignment, positive methylated and unmethylated controls, plate/batch, and replicate agreement. Never infer sample methylation from library concentration.
